recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13685 unless a new current-version issue changes leap-second policy or wording.
issue_request: FHIR-13685 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core datatypes issue requesting that time-bearing values support leap seconds by allowing seconds value 60, with regex updates for dateTime/timestamp and warning text about leap-second handling.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git-svn commit f2b3f28b2ff336fda895e176b2bdb2690ade688b, which explicitly references #13685/#13684 and updates primitive date/time regexes to include seconds value 60. Jira's final comment cites svn revision 12460, matching that commit.
additional_context: In current source, the relevant timestamp-like primitive is instant. The active primitive definitions in source/datatypes/primitives.xml retain leap-second support for instant, dateTime, and time. Later dateTime regex refinements and the existing FHIR-14094 audit on the combined branch did not remove that support.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current regexes already include `([0-5][0-9]|60)` for instant, dateTime, and time, and the datatype page says leap seconds are allowed while warning that many systems and libraries do not support them.

related_jiras.note: Co-implemented in the same 2017 regex commit, but it concerns year-zero validation rather than leap seconds.
Related STU3 dateTime schema regex audit already represented on the combined branch; used only as context.
